name: Egyptian Ratscrew
description: Egyptian Ratscrew (ERS) is a high-energy, reflex-based card game combining War-style card playing with a social 'slapping' mechanic. Players take turns playing one card face-up to a central pile; when specific combinations appear (pairs, sandwiches, sequences, top-bottom matches, etc.), all players race to slap the pile. The fastest player takes all the pile's cards. The goal is to collect all 52 cards.

content.text: Egyptian Ratscrew (ERS) is a high-energy, reflex-based card game combining War-style card playing with a social 'slapping' mechanic. Players take turns playing one card face-up to a central pile; when specific combinations appear (pairs, sandwiches, sequences, top-bottom matches, etc.), all players race to slap the pile. The fastest player takes all the pile's cards. The goal is to collect all 52 cards.
Egyptian Ratscrew is a 20th-century American game derived from the British game Egyptian Rat Pack and the classic Slapjack. The 'Egyptian' name may be a humorous Americanism unrelated to Egypt.
Two or more players; typically 2 to 7. The number of players is limited only by each participant's ability to reach the central pile. Cards are dealt as evenly as possible.
Deal entire deck evenly. Players do not look at their cards; hold them face-down.

items.text: Simple Slapjack Variant: Only Jacks trigger slaps. Simpler for younger players.
Extended Slap Rules: Add: Four-in-a-row, Same-suit sequence, Any two-card sum = 10, etc. House rules are unlimited.
